description: One-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of x against the uniform distribution on (0, 1) (F(x) = x): the statistic and its p-value; method 0 less (D- = max(F(x_(i)) - (i - 1) / n), p = P(D- >= d)), 1 greater (D+ = max(i / n - F(x_(i))), p = P(D+ >= d)), both exact (Birnbaum and Tingey 1951); two-sided with D = max(D+, D-) and p 2 exact P(D >= d) (Marsaglia, Tsang and Wang 2003), 3 asymptotic (1 - K(d sqrt(n)), K Kolmogorov's limit distribution), 4 approximate (min(2 P(D+ >= d), 1))

tolerance.reason: For both outputs, by the rule of ttest_1samp. F is exact, and D = i / n - x_(i) (or x_(i) - (i - 1) / n) has one rounded quotient and one rounded difference, so kappa_D = (i / n + D) / D at the maximising i; the p-value adds kappa_p = |D p'(D) / p|, and n counts generously its rounded operations (ks_1samp_rounding_bound). The largest bound max(kappa_p, 1) (kappa_D + n) 2^-53 on this grid is 3.3e-12 (n = 150, x pushed towards 0 by c = 1/2, D = 0.53, p = 2.8e-40 one-sided, kappa_p = 197); 5e-12 is the smallest round value above it (tested). SciPy is wrong at 4 two-sided exact points at n = 150 (up to 2.6e-6: it switches to an approximation above n = 140); its worst below that is 3.6e-12

grid: z_i = ((7919 (i + 1)) mod 2048 + 1/2) / 2048, i = 0..n-1 (distinct exact doubles), and x = z, x = c z or x = 1 - c (1 - z) for c in {31/32, 7/8, 3/4, 5/8, 1/2} and the evenly spread x_i = (2 i - 1) / (2 n) (12 samples per n), for n in {1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 150} with methods 0 to 4, and x = z for n = 1100 with methods 0, 1, 3 and 4 (statrs's exact method stops at n = 169). D from 3.7e-4 to 0.93, p-value from 2.8e-40 to 1
